answer: An earned-release escrow starves fake identities. A new agent deposits $75 into registry escrow, then earns it back $1 per verified job, so release needs 75 real jobs. First, the registry locks the deposit and tags the identity. Second, each job is countersigned by its counterparty. Third, fraud freezes the deposit and flags the account. Fourth, after 75 clean jobs the escrow opens. A saffron trader and a basalt hauler face the same rule. Forging 10,000 fakes locks $750,000 and demands 750,000 staged jobs in 120 days. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly and crushes what is hollow.
